samples.summary: REST contract changes are documented only in `docs/design/sheets/sheet.md`, not in the canonical REST design doc
samples.evidence: `docs/design/rest-api.md` §5.4 is where the v1 structural API's contract lives: line 278 states "Each endpoint echoes back the request it applied", and lines 306-318 enumerate "Two deliberate differences from the editor", the second of which is exactly the existing merge-split 409. This change adds a third deliberate difference (`POST .../move` now 409s when the resulting merge map would straddle the freeze), makes `POST .../insert` / `POST .../delete` silently grow (or release) the tab's frozen rows/columns — so those endpoints no longer merely echo "the request applied" — changes `PUT .../freeze` to answer with a snapped boundary that may differ from the requested one, adds a 409 to `PUT .../merges`, and adds two new 400s to `parseMerges` (entry count and total covered cells). None of that reaches `rest-api.md`; it is recorded only in `docs/design/sheets/sheet.md` (lines 129-143), which is the engine doc, not the API contract doc. A REST client reading the documented contract will still expect freeze to echo its request and merges to be bounded only per-span. Cost stays inside documentation accuracy, hence minor, but it is a design-doc-discipline violation: the change is filed against the wrong canonical doc for half of what it does.

samples.summary: `YorkieStore.setMerge`'s new refusal contract is not reflected in the frontend design doc's store table
samples.evidence: `docs/design/sheets/sheet.md` line 325 was updated to `setMerge(anchor, span): Promise<boolean>` and the prose explains that the store may refuse a block. `docs/design/frontend.md` line 291 still describes `setMerge(anchor, span)` as unconditionally "Write to `root.sheets[tabId].merges[anchorSref]`", which is now false: `YorkieStore.setMerge` spends a merge budget and can return `false` without writing, and it also now maintains batch-level merge state (`batchMerges`) that the table's batching description does not mention. Frontend.md is the canonical doc for the `YorkieStore` mapping table, so the store-side half of this change has no design-doc record.

samples.summary: The freeze-straddle scan is written twice in the backend instead of being one shared engine helper
samples.evidence: `ApiV1WorksheetController.assertMergesClearOfFreeze` and `ApiV1WorksheetStructureController.assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze` are the same loop — build the range with `toMergeRange(parseRef(anchorSref), span)`, test `crossesFreezePane`, throw a 409 naming the anchor — differing only in where the merge map comes from and in the message wording. The change otherwise takes care to put the shared predicate (`crossesFreezePane`, `snapFreezePastMerges`, `mergeBudgetAdmits`) in `packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/merging.ts` so engine and backend cannot drift; a `firstMergeCrossingFreeze(merges, rows, cols)` helper beside them would have done the same for this pair. As written the two 409 messages and the two scans can diverge independently, though both currently behave identically, so the cost is confined to the codebase.
searchedFor: Read of both backend controller hunks in the diff

samples.summary: The change bundles several independently-shippable concerns (rangeOf argument-spread fix, copy-buffer lifetime/revalidation, merge budget caps, freeze snapping, paste merge propagation) into one diff
samples.evidence: No originating issue text accompanies this review, so I cannot map hunks to acceptance criteria; judged against the design doc alone, the diff carries at least five separable features: the `rangeOf` fold rewrite in `model/core/coordinates.ts` (a stack-overflow/perf fix unrelated to merges or freeze), the copy-buffer lifetime change plus `revalidateCopyBuffer` for remote edits in `sheet.ts` / `view/worksheet.ts` (a clipboard-semantics change that removes `clearCopyBuffer()` after every paste in two view files), the three-way merge budget with load-time clamping in `rebuildMergeCoverMap`, the freeze/merge invariant across engine and v1 API, and merged-block propagation on copy/paste. Each is documented in `docs/design/sheets/sheet.md`, so nothing is undocumented, but the breadth makes the change hard to review or revert per-feature and makes it impossible for me to confirm scope against a stated outcome. Flagging as scope breadth, not as a defect in any one part.

samples.summary: ~140 lines of new prose about freeze snapping, merge budgets and the `Store.setMerge` contract are appended inside the single "Copy/paste" bullet
samples.evidence: The added block under the `**Copy/paste**` responsibility bullet (starting around line 96) covers the freeze-straddle invariant, `MaxSnappedFreeze`, the three merge-map ceilings, the load-path clamp in `rebuildMergeCoverMap`, the v1 API's 409/snap behavior, and `Store.setMerge`'s boolean contract. The file already has a `**Merged cells**` responsibility bullet (line 78) and a `Store` interface section (line ~322) where those belong. Filing into the canonical doc is right; nesting unrelated subsystems under Copy/paste makes the doc harder to navigate and to keep true.
